_comment_animal: which animal the data is: fly or mouse. It picks the modules that read the config and build the datasets (flyllm/animals.py)
_comment_trainfilestr: names of files containing training and validation data, made by mousellm/convert_mabe22.py. test.npz, the held-out test set, is not used in training
_comment_savedir: how often to save trained models
_comment_categories: categories to train on; the mouse data has none
_comment_simplify: subset of outputs and inputs to use, used while debugging
_comment_compute_sensory_diffs: whether to compute sensory diffs as additional inputs. not yet implemented.
_comment_flatten_labels: whether to string out labels into multiple tokens per timepoint
_comment_flatten_obs_idx: how to divide observations into separate tokens per timepoint. if sensory, then each type of sensory data is a token
_comment_flatten_do_separate_inputs: whether to separate the input features used by different input types for flattened models
_comment_discreteidx: which label indices should be discretized: the global movement, forward, sideways and turn
_comment_discretize_nbins: number of bins to discretize each output into
_comment_all_discretize_epsilon: smallest bin for each label, related to tracking noise, in cm/frame and rad/frame: about the still-mouse noise in a center step, 0.27 px or 0.037 cm per frame (step0/tracking_noise.py in the project dir)
_comment_discretize_epsilon: smallest bin for discretized outputs. if null, will use all_discretize_epsilon
_comment_contextl: number of timepoints of context during training: 256 frames is 8.5 s at 30 Hz; sequences are 1800 frames
_comment_masktype: if mlm model, type of masking to do. options: ind, block, null
_comment_max_mask_length: how long to mask out at a time (maximum) if masktype = block
_comment_pmask: probability of masking if masktype = ind
_comment_num_warmup_epochs: number of epochs, possibly fractional, over which the learning rate rises linearly to its full value at the start of training
_comment_lr_gpu_scaling: how the learning rate scales with the number of GPUs trained on, whose batches add up to the effective batch size: sqrt, times the square root of the GPU count, or linear, times the GPU count, which usually needs warmup
_comment_modeltype: mlm for masked model, clm for causal
_comment_modelstatetype: depricated? whether to try to fit discrete states as part of the model. this did not work. options: null, prob, best
_comment_pdropout_past: probability of dropping out labels as inputs
_comment_nstates: deprecated? if learning discrete states as part of the model, how many to learn
_comment_minstateprob: deprecated? if learning discrete states, state probabilities were going to 0, epsilon added to probability for a state
_comment_niterplot: how often (in training iterations) to plot debugging plots
_comment_model_nickname: nickname used when saving files related to this model.
_comment_compute_pose_vel: whether to predict the relative pose velocity (true) or position (false)
_comment_float32_matmul_precision: float32 matmul precision passed to torch.set_float32_matmul_precision: 'highest' is full fp32, 'high' allows TF32 on Ampere and newer GPUs (much faster)
_comment_use_autocast: whether to run model forward passes during training and validation under torch.autocast with dtype autocast_dtype (much faster); weights, optimizer state, and losses stay float32
_comment_autocast_dtype: dtype used for autocast if use_autocast is true, e.g. 'bfloat16'; ignored otherwise
_comment_val_epoch: compute the validation loss every val_epoch epochs (and always after the last epoch)
_comment_use_compile: whether to run model forward passes during training and validation through torch.compile (1.27x as fast per step on an A6000, but no faster on an H100, and compiling takes about a minute at the start of training)
_comment_use_sdpa_math_kernel: whether to run training and validation under sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH), restricting attention to PyTorch's unfused implementation; this was needed to avoid nans in training, but is slower than the fused kernels PyTorch otherwise chooses
_comment_conv2d_fc_as_linear: whether a conv2d observation embedding computes its final Conv2d layer, whose kernel spans a full input dimension, e.g. (1, 72), as the equivalent F.linear on the same weights (much faster, since cuDNN's backward for that convolution is very slow); false runs the Conv2d itself. Saved models are the same either way
_comment_num_workers: number of background worker processes for the training and validation DataLoaders (0 = load in the main process)
_comment_dataset_cache_dir: directory for caching the preprocessed training and validation datasets, so later runs with the same data config load them instead of rebuilding them (relative paths are relative to the working directory). null = no caching.
_comment_output_categories: categories for which predictions are penalized during training/test. if empty, all categories are used
_comment_augment_flip: whether to mirror the mice left to right for data augmentation
_comment_optimize_bins: parameters related to optimizing bin edges
_comment_bin_edges_absolute: bin edges for each discretized label, keyed by feature index, from optimal binning (flyllm/batch_optimal_binning.py). Empty means bins are fit from the data
